{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_bdrk_01C8FKeam88fJrcuRzM2b9GR","type":"tool_result","content":"1\t# Eval harness — rubric, test prompts, protocol\n2\t\n3\tMeasures whether a produced BUILD PLAN actually follows the skill. {"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-opus-5-5","id":"msg_bdrk_smlrp6rfp42yryhk7msk7qrvj24mxaopbdg33rarojef2xdo6tja","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"# BUILD PLAN: CI/CD platform for 50 microservices\n\n## 1. Classification\n- **What:** A shared build, test, sign, promote and deploy platform that 50 microservices run on. It replaces 50 separate pipelines.\n- **Type:** Infra. There are no AI components.\n- **Dominant constraint:** Correctness and integrity of what reaches prod. Scale (50 services × 3 environments, with many commits a day) comes second.\n- **Worst failure:** The platform pushes an unverified or compromised artifact to prod across many services at once. A shared platform multiplies blast radius, so one bad template or one leaked credential can affect all 50 services. Close behind: the platform is down and nobody can ship a hotfix.\n\n## 2. Tradeoff gates (resolved up front)\n\n| Decision | Default (chosen now) | Flip condition |\n|---|---|---|\n| Consistency vs availability | **Consistency for deploy state.** Git is the single source of truth for what runs where (GitOps). If the CD controller finds diverged or uncertain state, it stops rather than guessing. Builds favor availability: they retry and can run on any runner. | Git-host outages block hotfixes more than once a quarter. Then add an audited break-glass deploy path. Git still stays canonical. |\n| Monolith vs services (the platform itself) | **One shared platform:** one versioned library of reusable workflows and one CD controller. Not 50 bespoke pipelines. | More than about 20% of services need escape hatches the templates can't express. Then split templates by archetype (stateless, stateful, batch) instead of adding flags. |\n| Repo topology (for the 50 services) | **Keep the current polyrepo layout.** Services pull in the shared template library by pinned version. | Cross-repo atomic changes become frequent (more than about 1 per week blocked on coordination). Then evaluate a monorepo with Bazel or Nx. |\n| Sync vs async | **CI is synchronous and gates PR merge. CD is asynchronous and pull-based:** Argo CD reconciles from the config repo, so CI never holds prod credentials. | Some deploy targets can't run a pull agent (Lambda, legacy VMs). Those get push deploys using short-lived OIDC credentials, scoped per target. |\n| Artifact model | **Build once and promote the same immutable image digest** through dev, staging and prod. Environment differences live only in config overlays. | Effectively never. If a service needs a rebuild per environment, fix the service. |\n| Build vs buy | **Buy or adopt:** GitHub Actions (CI), Argo CD (CD), a managed registry (ECR or GHCR), Sigstore/cosign (signing), Kyverno (admission policy), Trivy (scanning). **Build only the glue:** templates, the promotion policy, the `service.yaml` contract and onboarding automation. | Hosted CI minutes cost more than the total cost of running our own runners, or compliance requires air-gapped builds. Then move to self-hosted ephemeral runners (Actions Runner Controller). |\n| Deploy target | **Kubernetes, with one cluster per environment.** This is stated as an assumption, not left silent. | An inventory shows more than about 10% of services on a different target. Then add a target-abstraction step to the CD layer before fleet onboarding (Phase 4). |\n| (AI) prompt+RAG vs fine-tune | N/A: there is no AI component. | — |\n| (AI) hosted API vs self-host | N/A: there is no AI component. | — |\n\n## 3. Walking skeleton (Phase 0)\nFor CI/CD, the \"request\" is a commit and the \"response\" is that commit running in prod and serving real traffic.\n\n- **The real request:** Merge a one-line change to one real, low-risk, stateless service, picked as service #1.\n- **Tiers it crosses:**\n  1. GitHub (branch protection on `main`)\n  2. CI runner\n  3. Container build (base image pinned by digest)\n  4. Unit tests\n  5. Push to registry by digest\n  6. Keyless cosign signature\n  7. Bot PR bumping the digest in the `deploy-config` repo\n  8. Argo CD syncs to **staging**\n  9. Smoke test\n  10. Promotion PR (human approves)\n  11. Argo CD syncs to **prod**\n  12. Kubernetes readiness check\n  13. The service returns the new version on `/version`\n- **Deployment:** The platform's own pieces (registry, Argo CD, IAM roles, OIDC trust) are created with Terraform from a `platform-infra` repo. No click-ops, even on day zero.\n- **Logging and monitoring on day zero:**\n  - Every pipeline stage emits an OpenTelemetry span, with commit SHA and digest as attributes.\n  - Argo CD metrics go to Prometheus.\n  - Deploy events appear as annotations on the service's Grafana dashboard.\n  - An alert fires on a failed Argo sync or a failed pipeline on `main`.\n  - Lead time (commit to prod) is recorded as the first DORA metric.\n- **Exit check:**\n  - The merged change is serving in prod.\n  - One trace shows every stage from commit to prod.\n  - The lead-time metric is visible on a dashboard.\n  - A `git revert` in `deploy-config` rolls prod back, and that rollback has been demonstrated, not just assumed.\n\n## 4. Phases (ordered by dependency; within a phase, widest blast radius first)\n\n**Phase 0: Walking skeleton.** See Section 3.\n\n**Phase 1: Trust and contract substrate**\n- **Unlocks:** Any service can be described to the platform, and every artifact can be traced to its origin.\n- **Depends on:** The Phase 0 path running end to end in prod.\n- **Tasks** (widest blast radius first):\n  1. **Identity and authorization model.** OIDC federation from CI to the cloud, with no static keys anywhere.\n     - Role split: CI can only push to the registry. Argo can only deploy. Humans have no direct write access to prod.\n     - If this is wrong, every later phase gets rewired, so it goes first.\n  2. **Artifact contract.**\n     - Images are referenced by digest. Tags are informational only.\n     - Every image gets an SBOM (Syft) and SLSA provenance.\n     - Every image is cosign-signed.\n  3. **Service contract (`service.yaml`).** Each service declares owner, tier (1–3), archetype, build entrypoint, test entrypoint, health endpoint and whether it is stateful. The file is validated against a JSON Schema.\n  4. **Layout of the `deploy-config` repo.** Structure is `apps/<service>/{base,overlays/{dev,staging,prod}}` using Kustomize.\n  5. **Ephemeral runners.** A fresh runner per job. Self-hosted runners only where tests need private network access.\n- **Exit check:**\n  - Service #1 is rebuilt using only OIDC, and every static CI secret has been deleted.\n  - Kyverno verifies signatures in **audit** mode and reports 100% of prod images signed.\n  - `service.yaml` validation fails a PR when a required field is missing.\n\n**Phase 2: Golden-path templates and a pilot group of 5 services**\n- **Unlocks:** Services with different shapes can onboard without writing platform code.\n- **Depends on:** The Phase 1 contracts, proven on service #1.\n- **Tasks** (widest blast radius first):\n  1. **Versioning and rollout for the templates themselves.**\n     - The reusable workflow library is semver'd, and consumers pin to a version.\n     - Renovate opens the version-bump PRs.\n     - New template versions go to 1 service, then the pilot group, then everyone.\n     - A template change reaches all 50 services, so this mechanism comes first.\n  2. **Database migration pattern for stateful services.**\n     - Migrations run as a separate job that must finish before rollout.\n     - Expand/contract only, so the previous version still runs against the new schema.\n     - A wrong pattern here means data loss, so it comes before the language-specific work.\n  3. **Build archetypes.** Pick 5 pilot services that cover at least 3 languages, plus one stateful service and one batch job.\n  4. **Build caching.** Layer cache plus a dependency proxy or mirror.\n  5. **PR checks.** Lint, unit tests, Trivy scan, secret scan.\n- **Exit check:**\n  - All 5 pilot services deploy to prod through the templates with zero per-service pipeline code.\n  - One template release has gone 1 → 5 services and been rolled back, with rollback proven.\n  - One stateful migration has shipped with the old version still serving.\n\n**Phase 3: Promotion, policy and safe rollback**\n- **Unlocks:** Prod deploys are safe enough to let the fleet onboard.\n- **Depends on:** Templates proven on varied services, and signing and provenance proven in audit mode.\n- **Tasks** (widest blast radius first):\n  1. **Promotion policy as code.** Only a digest that is signed, has provenance, passed tests and passed staging can be promoted. The policy is evaluated in the promotion PR check.\n  2. **Switch Kyverno to enforce in prod.** Unsigned images or images without provenance are rejected at admission.\n  3. **Automated rollback.**\n     - Argo health checks plus error-rate and latency checks after deploy.\n     - On failure, a bot reverts the change in `deploy-config`.\n  4. **Approval rules by tier.** Tier 1 needs two-person approval. Tiers 2–3 auto-promote after staging soak.\n  5. **Deploy freeze switch and audited break-glass path.**\n- **Exit check:**\n  - A deliberately broken release is reverted automatically within 5 minutes.\n  - An unsigned image is rejected in prod.\n  - A break-glass deploy works and raises an alert.\n\n**Phase 4: Fleet onboarding (5 → 50)**\n- **Unlocks:** The whole organization is on one paved path, and the legacy pipelines are retired.\n- **Depends on:** The promotion and rollback safety net from Phase 3.\n- **Tasks** (platform work widest first):\n  1. **Onboarding automation.** A scaffolder opens a PR containing `service.yaml`, the workflow call and the Argo app. It also generates the service catalog from `service.yaml`.\n  2. **Capacity for 50 services × 3 environments (about 150 Argo apps).**\n     - Runner autoscaling with a minimum warm pool.\n     - Concurrency limits per repo.\n     - Handling for GitHub API rate limits.\n     - Argo CD in HA mode, with controller sharding if needed.\n  3. **Onboarding waves.** Tier 3 first, then tier 2, then tier 1. This is a deliberate exception to \"widest first\": the waves validate the platform, so the lowest-risk services go through it first.\n  4. **Legacy cleanup.** Delete each old pipeline and revoke its credentials as each service cuts over.\n- **Exit check:**\n  - 50 of 50 services are on the platform.\n  - Zero legacy pipelines or credentials remain.\n  - p95 commit-to-staging time is under 15 minutes.\n  - The platform has been restored from Terraform and Git in a disaster-recovery drill.\n\n**Phase 5: Progressive delivery and optimization**\n- **Unlocks:** Safer tier-1 releases, faster CI and cost control.\n- **Depends on:** Trustworthy per-service metrics and SLOs, which only exist once the fleet emits them uniformly (Phase 4).\n- **Tasks** (widest blast radius first):\n  1. Argo Rollouts canaries for tier-1 services, with automated analysis against SLO metrics.\n  2. Flaky-test detection and quarantine.\n  3. Test-impact analysis. It falls back to the full test suite if it is uncertain.\n  4. DORA dashboard and cost-per-pipeline reporting.\n- **Exit check:**\n  - Tier-1 services ship through canaries that abort automatically.\n  - Change-failure rate and MTTR are reported weekly.\n\n## 5. Cross-cutting concerns (per phase, from the first commit)\n\n| Phase | Security | Observability | Reproducibility | Resilience |\n|---|---|---|---|---|\n| 0 | OIDC to the registry from day one, with no static keys. Branch protection on `main` and `deploy-config`. Secrets in a secrets manager. | An OTel span per pipeline stage. Argo metrics in Prometheus. Deploy annotations on Grafana. Alerts on sync or pipeline failure. Lead-time metric. | Base image pinned by digest. Actions pinned by SHA. Lockfiles. Platform infra in Terraform. Build once, promote the digest. | Rollback by `git revert`, demonstrated. A documented manual break-glass deploy of the last known-good manifest. |\n| 1 | Least-privilege role split. Keyless signing. SBOM and SLSA provenance. Kyverno in audit mode. | Every role assumption is logged to the SIEM. A metric for signature-verification results. | `service.yaml` validated against a schema. Builds get network access only through the dependency proxy. | Ephemeral runners, so a poisoned runner can't persist. Registry replication or pull-through cache. |\n| 2 | Trivy and secret scanning in the templates. Pinned template versions, so a compromised template can't spread silently. | Success rate and duration broken down by template version, so a bad template rollout is visible. | Semver'd templates bumped by Renovate. Rebuilding the same commit gives the same dependency set. | Template rollout 1 → pilot → all, with rollback. Retries only on known-transient steps. Expand/contract migrations. |\n| 3 | Signatures and provenance enforced at prod admission. Policy-as-code promotion. Two-person rule for tier 1. Break-glass alerts. | A queryable deploy audit trail (who, which digest, when, which policy decision). Change-failure rate and MTTR. | Environments differ only through declared Kustomize overlays. Argo drift detection. | Automated rollback on failed health or SLO checks. Deploy freeze switch. Runbook for when the platform is down. |\n| 4 | Secrets scoped per service. Legacy credentials revoked at each cutover. | Fleet dashboard: per-service lead time, queue time, runner saturation. | Onboarding is generated by the scaffolder, not hand-tuned. | Runner autoscaling with a warm minimum. Concurrency limits. Argo HA and sharding. Disaster-recovery restore drill. |\n| 5 | Quarterly access review. Aim for SLSA Level 3 build provenance. | Canary analysis metrics. Cost per pipeline. Flaky-test rates. | Test-impact analysis is deterministic and falls back to the full suite. | Canaries abort automatically. Chaos drills: kill Argo, simulate a registry outage. |\n\n## 6. AI layer\nN/A. This is a pure infra system with no model, retrieval or agent components. If the platform later adds AI features (for example LLM-generated PR summaries or failure triage), run this skill's AI layer for that feature, starting with guardrails and budgets.\n\n## 7. Deliberately deferred\n- **Ephemeral preview environments per PR.** Pull forward when review or QA cycle time becomes the top bottleneck and the cluster cost per preview is approved.\n- **Monorepo migration (Bazel or Nx).** Pull forward when the repo-topology gate's flip condition fires.\n- **Multi-region or multi-cluster CD (ApplicationSets across clusters).** Pull forward when prod goes multi-region.\n- **Self-hosting all runners.** Pull forward when the build-vs-buy gate's flip condition fires (cost or air-gap requirements).\n- **Canaries for tier-2 and tier-3 services.** Pull forward per service once it has a defined SLO and a clean metrics history.\n- **A full developer portal (Backstage).** For now, a catalog generated from `service.yaml` is enough. Pull forward when teams report discoverability or ownership problems that the generated catalog can't solve.\n- **Bit-for-bit hermetic builds (Bazel or Nix).** Pull forward when compliance requires SLSA Level 4 or reproducibility audits.\n- **A custom pipeline DSL or orchestrator.** Not planned. Pull forward only if GitHub Actions reusable workflows provably can't express a pattern that more than 10 services need.\n\n## 8. Eval score: **19/20**\n\n| # | Dimension | Score | Note |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| 1 | Dependency ordering | 2 | Each phase names the proven thing it depends on. Enforcement only follows audit mode, and canaries only follow uniform metrics. |\n| 2 | Walking skeleton first | 2 | One real commit goes all the way to prod, with a trace, a metric and a demonstrated rollback before any feature work. |\n| 3 | Tradeoff gates up front | 2 | Seven gates, each with a default and a flip condition. Walking skeleton (Phase 0)\nFor CI/CD, the \"request\" is a commit and the \"response\" is that commit running in prod and serving real traffic.\n\n- **The real request:** Merge a one-line change to one real, low-risk, stateless service, picked as service #1.\n- **Tiers it crosses:**\n  1. GitHub (branch protection on `main`)\n  2. CI runner\n  3. Container build (base image pinned by digest)\n  4. Unit tests\n  5. Push to registry by digest\n  6. Keyless cosign signature\n  7. Bot PR bumping the digest in the `deploy-config` repo\n  8. Argo CD syncs to **staging**\n  9. Smoke test\n  10. Promotion PR (human approves)\n  11. Argo CD syncs to **prod**\n  12. Kubernetes readiness check\n  13. The service returns the new version on `/version`\n- **Deployment:** The platform's own pieces (registry, Argo CD, IAM roles, OIDC trust) are created with Terraform from a `platform-infra` repo. No click-ops, even on day zero.\n- **Logging and monitoring on day zero:**\n  - Every pipeline stage emits an OpenTelemetry span, with commit SHA and digest as attributes.\n  - Argo CD metrics go to Prometheus.\n  - Deploy events appear as annotations on the service's Grafana dashboard.\n  - An alert fires on a failed Argo sync or a failed pipeline on `main`.\n  - Lead time (commit to prod) is recorded as the first DORA metric.\n- **Exit check:**\n  - The merged change is serving in prod.\n  - One trace shows every stage from commit to prod.\n  - The lead-time metric is visible on a dashboard.\n  - A `git revert` in `deploy-config` rolls prod back, and that rollback has been demonstrated, not just assumed.\n\n## 4. Phases (ordered by dependency; within a phase, widest blast radius first)\n\n**Phase 0: Walking skeleton.** See Section 3.\n\n**Phase 1: Trust and contract substrate**\n- **Unlocks:** Any service can be described to the platform, and every artifact can be traced to its origin.\n- **Depends on:** The Phase 0 path running end to end in prod.\n- **Tasks** (widest blast radius first):\n  1. **Identity and authorization model.** OIDC federation from CI to the cloud, with no static keys anywhere.\n     - Role split: CI can only push to the registry. Argo can only deploy. Humans have no direct write access to prod.\n     - If this is wrong, every later phase gets rewired, so it goes first.\n  2. **Artifact contract.**\n     - Images are referenced by digest. Tags are informational only.\n     - Every image gets an SBOM (Syft) and SLSA provenance.\n     - Every image is cosign-signed.\n  3. **Service contract (`service.yaml`).** Each service declares owner, tier (1–3), archetype, build entrypoint, test entrypoint, health endpoint and whether it is stateful. The file is validated against a JSON Schema.\n  4. **Layout of the `deploy-config` repo.** Structure is `apps/<service>/{base,overlays/{dev,staging,prod}}` using Kustomize.\n  5. **Ephemeral runners.** A fresh runner per job. Self-hosted runners only where tests need private network access.\n- **Exit check:**\n  - Service #1 is rebuilt using only OIDC, and every static CI secret has been deleted.\n  - Kyverno verifies signatures in **audit** mode and reports 100% of prod images signed.\n  - `service.yaml` validation fails a PR when a required field is missing.\n\n**Phase 2: Golden-path templates and a pilot group of 5 services**\n- **Unlocks:** Services with different shapes can onboard without writing platform code.\n- **Depends on:** The Phase 1 contracts, proven on service #1.\n- **Tasks** (widest blast radius first):\n  1. **Versioning and rollout for the templates themselves.**\n     - The reusable workflow library is semver'd, and consumers pin to a version.\n     - Renovate opens the version-bump PRs.\n     - New template versions go to 1 service, then the pilot group, then everyone.\n     - A template change reaches all 50 services, so this mechanism comes first.\n  2. **Database migration pattern for stateful services.**\n     - Migrations run as a separate job that must finish before rollout.\n     - Expand/contract only, so the previous version still runs against the new schema.\n     - A wrong pattern here means data loss, so it comes before the language-specific work.\n  3. **Build archetypes.** Pick 5 pilot services that cover at least 3 languages, plus one stateful service and one batch job.\n  4. **Build caching.** Layer cache plus a dependency proxy or mirror.\n  5. **PR checks.** Lint, unit tests, Trivy scan, secret scan.\n- **Exit check:**\n  - All 5 pilot services deploy to prod through the templates with zero per-service pipeline code.\n  - One template release has gone 1 → 5 services and been rolled back, with rollback proven.\n  - One stateful migration has shipped with the old version still serving.\n\n**Phase 3: Promotion, policy and safe rollback**\n- **Unlocks:** Prod deploys are safe enough to let the fleet onboard.\n- **Depends on:** Templates proven on varied services, and signing and provenance proven in audit mode.\n- **Tasks** (widest blast radius first):\n  1. **Promotion policy as code.** Only a digest that is signed, has provenance, passed tests and passed staging can be promoted. The policy is evaluated in the promotion PR check.\n  2. **Switch Kyverno to enforce in prod.** Unsigned images or images without provenance are rejected at admission.\n  3. **Automated rollback.**\n     - Argo health checks plus error-rate and latency checks after deploy.\n     - On failure, a bot reverts the change in `deploy-config`.\n  4. **Approval rules by tier.** Tier 1 needs two-person approval. Tiers 2–3 auto-promote after staging soak.\n  5. **Deploy freeze switch and audited break-glass path.**\n- **Exit check:**\n  - A deliberately broken release is reverted automatically within 5 minutes.\n  - An unsigned image is rejected in prod.\n  - A break-glass deploy works and raises an alert.\n\n**Phase 4: Fleet onboarding (5 → 50)**\n- **Unlocks:** The whole organization is on one paved path, and the legacy pipelines are retired.\n- **Depends on:** The promotion and rollback safety net from Phase 3.\n- **Tasks** (platform work widest first):\n  1. **Onboarding automation.** A scaffolder opens a PR containing `service.yaml`, the workflow call and the Argo app. It also generates the service catalog from `service.yaml`.\n  2. **Capacity for 50 services × 3 environments (about 150 Argo apps).**\n     - Runner autoscaling with a minimum warm pool.\n     - Concurrency limits per repo.\n     - Handling for GitHub API rate limits.\n     - Argo CD in HA mode, with controller sharding if needed.\n  3. **Onboarding waves.** Tier 3 first, then tier 2, then tier 1. This is a deliberate exception to \"widest first\": the waves validate the platform, so the lowest-risk services go through it first.\n  4. **Legacy cleanup.** Delete each old pipeline and revoke its credentials as each service cuts over.\n- **Exit check:**\n  - 50 of 50 services are on the platform.\n  - Zero legacy pipelines or credentials remain.\n  - p95 commit-to-staging time is under 15 minutes.\n  - The platform has been restored from Terraform and Git in a disaster-recovery drill.\n\n**Phase 5: Progressive delivery and optimization**\n- **Unlocks:** Safer tier-1 releases, faster CI and cost control.\n- **Depends on:** Trustworthy per-service metrics and SLOs, which only exist once the fleet emits them uniformly (Phase 4).\n- **Tasks** (widest blast radius first):\n  1. Argo Rollouts canaries for tier-1 services, with automated analysis against SLO metrics.\n  2. Flaky-test detection and quarantine.\n  3. Test-impact analysis. It falls back to the full test suite if it is uncertain.\n  4. DORA dashboard and cost-per-pipeline reporting.\n- **Exit check:**\n  - Tier-1 services ship through canaries that abort automatically.\n  - Change-failure rate and MTTR are reported weekly.\n\n## 5. AI layer\nN/A. This is a pure infra system with no model, retrieval or agent components. If the platform later adds AI features (for example LLM-generated PR summaries or failure triage), run this skill's AI layer for that feature, starting with guardrails and budgets.\n\n## 7. Deliberately deferred\n- **Ephemeral preview environments per PR.** Pull forward when review or QA cycle time becomes the top bottleneck and the cluster cost per preview is approved.\n- **Monorepo migration (Bazel or Nx).** Pull forward when the repo-topology gate's flip condition fires.\n- **Multi-region or multi-cluster CD (ApplicationSets across clusters).** Pull forward when prod goes multi-region.\n- **Self-hosting all runners.** Pull forward when the build-vs-buy gate's flip condition fires (cost or air-gap requirements).\n- **Canaries for tier-2 and tier-3 services.** Pull forward per service once it has a defined SLO and a clean metrics history.\n- **A full developer portal (Backstage).** For now, a catalog generated from `service.yaml` is enough. Pull forward when teams report discoverability or ownership problems that the generated catalog can't solve.\n- **Bit-for-bit hermetic builds (Bazel or Nix).** Pull forward when compliance requires SLSA Level 4 or reproducibility audits.\n- **A custom pipeline DSL or orchestrator.** Not planned.
